description.value: An exploratory study used an emotional Stroop task during fMRI in healthy adolescent girls, fitting Hidden Markov models to behavioral data and testing voxelwise neural correlates of hidden states and reaction time.

spans.text: Here, we administered an emotional Stroop task to a sample of healthy adolescent girls (N = 24) during fMRI and used HMM to implement theoretical behavioral models.

value: We hypothesize that the model-based subprocesses of emotional conflict processing will be associated with similar neural mechanisms as the contrast-based measures of neural activity (dlPFC, pgACC, dACC, and anterior insula).
we hypothesize that activity of the dACC and anterior insula will be related to stimulus processing while activity in the dlPFC and pgACC will be associated with attentional control.

value: Longer reaction time was positively related to broad areas of activity in the bilateral anterior insula cortex, the dACC/pre-SMA, and bilateral caudate, and negatively related to activity in bilateral posterior insula. These findings were consistent with previous findings that activity in the cingulate and insula scales positively with reaction time, suggesting their role in sustained attention and awareness.
